explanation: [[kw:Fixed costs]] remain constant regardless of output (rent, insurance, salaries).
[[kw:Variable costs]] change directly with the quantity produced or sold (materials, direct labor).
Total Cost = Fixed Cost + (Variable Cost per unit × Quantity).
Knowing this split is essential for breakeven analysis.

formulaCard.title: Contribution Margin Formulas

explanation: [[kw:Contribution Margin (CM) per unit]] = Selling Price (SP) – Variable Cost (VC) per unit.
It is the amount each unit contributes to covering fixed costs.
After fixed costs are covered, CM becomes pure profit.
CM can also be expressed as a ratio: CM Ratio = CM per unit ÷ SP.
[[imp:CM ≠ profit; it first covers fixed costs.]]

hints: BEP units = Fixed costs ÷ CM per unit.

confusionCorner.body: Don't confuse contribution margin with gross profit. [[imp:Gross profit = Sales – Cost of Goods Sold (which includes only production costs). CM = SP – all variable costs, which may include selling expenses.]]

blocks.title: 3. Breakeven Point in Units

questions.prompt: Breakeven point in units = Fixed costs ÷ ___ per unit.
Fixed costs \$5,000, CM per unit \$25. Find BEP in units. (number only)
If BEP is 400 units and actual sales are 600, how many units contribute to profit? (number only)

explanation: [[kw:Breakeven Point (BEP) in units]] = Fixed Costs ÷ Contribution Margin per unit.
It is the number of units that must be sold so that total contribution margin exactly equals fixed costs.
Below BEP → loss; above BEP → profit (each additional unit adds its CM to profit).
Formula: $$\text{BEP (units)} = \frac{\text{Fixed Costs}}{\text{CM per unit}}$$.
BEP is a critical planning tool for businesses.

formulaCard.title: Breakeven Point in Units
notes: If units sold > BEP, profit = (units above BEP) × CM per unit.

visuals.caption: Higher fixed costs or lower CM means a higher breakeven volume.
visuals.title: Breakeven Calculation

visuals.caption: BEP in dollars is useful for comparing across product lines.
visuals.title: From Units to Dollars

explanation: [[kw:Breakeven Point in dollars (BEP $)]] = Fixed Costs ÷ CM Ratio.
CM Ratio = CM per unit ÷ Selling Price (or Total CM ÷ Total Sales for multi‑product).
This tells you the total sales revenue needed to cover all costs.
Useful when selling many products with different SPs — you just need the overall CM ratio.
Formula: $$\text{BEP }(\$) = \frac{\text{Fixed Costs}}{\text{CM Ratio}}$$.

notes: CM Ratio is always less than 1.
formulaCard.title: BEP in Dollars
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{BEP }(\$) = \frac{\text{Fixed Costs}}{\text{CM Ratio}}$$ $$\text{CM Ratio} = \frac{\text{CM per unit}}{\text{SP}} = \frac{\text{Total CM}}{\text{Total Sales}}$$

confusionCorner.body: The CM ratio must reflect the sales mix for multi‑product companies. [[imp:If the sales mix changes, the CM ratio changes, and BEP must be recalculated.]]
confusionCorner.title: Watch out!

challengeCorner.prompt: A business has fixed costs \$120,000 and a CM ratio of 0.30. It wants to earn a \$30,000 profit. What sales revenue is needed?

discoveryHook.scenario: The coffee shop also sells pastries with different prices. To find total sales revenue needed to break even, it uses the overall CM ratio. If the average CM ratio is 0.625, then BEP in dollars = \$2,000 ÷ 0.625 = \$3,200.

visuals.title: Backpack Blueprint
visuals.caption: Both unit and dollar BEP give consistent checks.

explanation: Blueprint steps for BEP problems:
1. Understand: identify fixed costs, selling price, variable cost per unit.
2. Solve: compute CM per unit, CM ratio, BEP in units, BEP in dollars.
3. Conclude: verify that at BEP, total CM equals fixed costs (profit zero).
This systematic approach prevents mix‑ups between units and dollars.

formulaCard.title: BEP Blueprint Formulas
notes: If profit target is given, add to fixed costs in numerator.
formulaCard.formula: $$\text{CM per unit} = \text{SP} - \text{VC}$$ $$\text{BEP (units)} = \frac{\text{FC}}{\text{CM per unit}}$$ $$\text{CM Ratio} = \frac{\text{CM per unit}}{\text{SP}}$$ $$\text{BEP (\$)} = \frac{\text{FC}}{\text{CM Ratio}}$$
